chapter: Teaching, radio and the WSMB band
title: Changing his name to Johnny Wiggs for WSMB radio
summary: He returned to jazz at WSMB in 1945 after teaching music, and took the name Johnny Wiggs so the school board would not object.

this reel Johnny Wiggs that that that was very recent that is say 17 years ago or something like that I was I'd been teaching school for 15 years and and I had quit teaching music and I felt sort of lost without music and I felt like going back to jazz I hadn't played jazz in maybe 20 years so I went up to see Teddy Fongloo remember he played terror patch with us in the invincibles he was at that time the 1945 he was the sales manager of WSMB so they had another band up there legitimate group of musicians and I said tell you why don't you why don't you give me a job up here give me give my band a job up here I can get a first-class jazz band together he said fine Johnny I'll see if I can't arrange it for you so the poor legitimate band got the skids and we went in and what was the question you asked me now oh wait why'd I change my name yeah well of course I know the school board would frown on me playing stuff stuff He said, fine, Johnny, I'll see if I can't arrange it for you.
So the poor legitimate man got the skids, and we went in. And what was the question you asked me now? Oh, yeah, why did I change my name?

Well, of course, I knew the school board would frown on me playing such lowly music and teaching their pupils, and they wouldn't work politically. Anyway, you know, to have a man playing such indecent music and teaching these saintly children, that were under the...
What about changing your name there when you went on the radio?

Oh, yeah, well, I knew the school board wouldn't like me to continue teaching for them and playing such disreputable music on the air. So I changed my name to Johnny Wiggs, Wiggs being the beginning of Wigington, W-I-G-G-S, beginning of my middle name. And nobody knew I was on there as a school teacher except a few of my friends.
